dossiers.facts: FSSR standardises quinoa as dried mature Chenopodium quinoa grain in Chapter 2.4 Cereals and Cereal Products. CTR IX cereal-grain lead/cadmium articles explicitly exclude quinoa; CTR aflatoxin article uses the distinct words cereal and cereal products.
dossiers.open_proof: Confirm whether the marketed quinoa grain is legally in the CTR cereal-and-cereal-products aflatoxin article; do not borrow the explicitly excluded lead/cadmium cereal-grain limits.

dossiers.facts: FSSR identifies chia Salvia hispanica as a mint-family seed. Listing within cereals standards does not itself prove named CTR oilseed or cereal applicability.
dossiers.open_proof: Obtain affirmative legal crop classification; no default cereal or oilseed aflatoxin figure.

dossiers.facts: Cube sugar is made from refined crystallised sugar. Its finished standard specifies total ash <=0.03%; CTR refined-white-sugar lead article requires sulphated ash <=0.03%, which is analytically distinct.
dossiers.open_proof: Confirm exact final refined sugar article and finished sulphated-ash result before assigning the CTR lead figure or chromium refined sugar article.

dossiers.facts: Misri may derive from any sugar or palmyrah juice; total ash <=0.4% is not proof of a specific refined sugar category or sulphated ash fraction.
dossiers.open_proof: Prove actual raw sugar source and marketed finished-article class; separately obtain sulphated ash if the claimed metal article requires it.

dossiers.facts: Dried glucose syrup FSSR sulphated ash is max 1.0%; CTR IX high-ash starch-conversion lead article requires more than 1.0%. These numerical criteria cannot be satisfied simultaneously by conforming dried glucose syrup.
dossiers.open_proof: Exclude the high-ash starch conversion lead row for a conforming lot; separately determine any actually applicable other named or conditional general article.
